strengths: The paper addresses a useful problem with an identifiable audience in representation learning, program analysis, and reverse engineering. Transferring information from aligned source code and comments into a representation usable without those inputs is a sensible research direction.

The combination of a fixed source/comment encoder, a trainable binary encoder, and learned interpolation is understandable at a high level. The component ablations provide preliminary evidence about the roles of comments and encoder anchoring.

Evaluation spans four task families and reports promising gains. For example, function-name accuracy increases from RoBERTa's 29.41% to 33.41%, and summarization BLEU-4 reaches 34.36 versus GraphCodeBERT's 32.43. Dataset counts, several fine-tuning settings, and qualitative examples help readers assess the experiments.
weaknesses: Necessary—align the claimed deployment setting with the evidence. Sections 3.1–3.2 evaluate compiler-produced LLVM IR, rather than representations recovered from stripped executables. These are not trivially interchangeable: compiler IR can preserve identifiers, types, and structure unavailable after compilation and stripping. Figures 7–8 visibly retain informative function and global names; only the function-name experiment explicitly describes function-name removal. Either demonstrate the claimed stripped-binary setting or restrict the conclusions to compiler-generated LLVM IR and document retained information.

Necessary—resolve the evaluation protocol. Table 2 gives POJ-104 disjoint sets of 64/16/24 problem labels, yet Sections 3.2 and 4.2 describe classification into 104 classes. An ordinary supervised classifier cannot learn held-out labels without an additional prediction or support-set mechanism. Specify whether this is retrieval, metric learning, or classification, including the training objective and evaluation procedure. Define MAP, MAR, and MAF1 precisely. Also reconcile Section 3.2's validation-set evaluation for AnghaBench with Section 4.3's test-set description and explain checkpoint selection.

Necessary—separate interpolation benefits from additional training. CONTRABIN-PCL receives 10 pretraining epochs, whereas the full model receives 30 or 70 depending on the task. The no-interpolation ablation also receives only 10 epochs; its asserted convergence is not demonstrated. Consequently, these comparisons do not isolate the central mechanism. Provide a control with matched training exposure and distinguish the contributions of linear interpolation, feature-wise interpolation, and their ordering, or narrow the component-level claims.

Necessary—make the method reproducible. Equation (4) omits the softmax described in the surrounding text, leaving unnormalized similarities as cross-entropy targets. Specify the actual target normalization, loss direction or symmetrization, temperature, and gradient flow through targets. The manuscript also needs the encoder architectures and initialization, tokenization and pooling, interpolation-network dimensions, and downstream decoder construction. Referring generally to SimpleCLIP settings does not resolve these choices.

Necessary—qualify claims of semantic correctness and comprehension. The only comment-generation procedure described uses CodeT5; clarify the provenance of downstream reference summaries and whether evaluation measures agreement with that generator. BLEU, GLEU, exact match, and a few examples do not establish functional correctness of reconstructed programs or the claimed long-range semantic robustness. Independent semantic checks are needed to retain those claims; otherwise, describe the findings as reference-text reconstruction performance.

Necessary—correct the embedding-analysis argument in Section 4.1. Unique programs can share semantics and legitimately form clusters, so uniqueness does not imply that clustering is erroneous. Neither fewer clusters nor distances between selected points in separately fitted t-SNE visualizations prove improved representation quality. Treat Figure 6 as exploratory illustration or support the interpretation with quantitative measurements in the original embedding space.

Necessary—calibrate comparative and robustness claims. Reverse-engineering results are mixed: GraphCodeBERT has higher BLEU-4, while CONTRABIN's exact-match advantage is only 0.43 percentage points. Single-seed results without uncertainty do not establish that these small differences are reliable. Report suitable uncertainty estimates or moderate the superiority and robustness claims. Acceptance need not depend on outperforming every baseline, but conclusions must match the evidence.

Optional—improve presentation consistency. Correct the DIRT/DIRE/DIRTY naming, references to three versus four downstream tasks, GLUE/GLEU terminology, and the ablation reference to Figure 7 instead of Table 7. These fixes would make the manuscript easier to follow.
